before.name: backup-demo.py
before.code:
import sqlite3, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    backup_path = Path(folder) / "backup.sqlite"
    source = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    source.executescript("CREATE TABLE notes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,title TEXT); INSERT INTO notes VALUES(1,'Moon'),(2,'Ocean');")
    source.commit()
    with sqlite3.connect(backup_path) as saved:
        source.backup(saved)
    source.close()
    with sqlite3.connect(backup_path) as restored:
        assert restored.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok"
        assert restored.execute("SELECT id,title FROM notes ORDER BY id").fetchall() == [(1,"Moon"),(2,"Ocean")]
    print("Disposable backup reopened and verified")

after.name: backup-demo.py
after.code:
import sqlite3, tempfile
from contextlib import closing
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    backup_path = Path(folder) / "backup.sqlite"
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(":memory:")) as source:
        source.executescript("CREATE TABLE notes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,title TEXT); INSERT INTO notes VALUES(1,'Moon'),(2,'Ocean');")
        source.commit()
        with closing(sqlite3.connect(backup_path)) as saved:
            source.backup(saved)
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(backup_path)) as restored:
        assert restored.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok"
        assert restored.execute("SELECT id,title FROM notes ORDER BY id").fetchall() == [(1,"Moon"),(2,"Ocean")]
    print("Disposable backup reopened and verified")

reason: Windows runtime exposed unclosed SQLite connections during temporary-directory cleanup. contextlib.closing closes source and both backup connections even if assertions fail.
